statement: BC should balance the provincial budget by cutting spending.

passages.title: CPBC Policy Declaration (March 2025)
passages.quote:
Fix the Budget
 4.03 The Conservative Party of British Columbia commits to supporting a return to balanced provincial budgets at
 the earliest practical opportunity.
 4.04 The Conservative Party of British Columbia will maintain balanced budgets over the long term, except in
 times of extraordinary circumstances such as provincial emergencies or economic recessions, with a clear
 plan for recovery to fiscal balance in such cases.
 4.05 Program Review: All existing or planned programs administered by the government, Crown corporations and
 other organizations owned, controlled or supported by the Government of British Columbia must be reviewed
 to determine if they are meeting performance

passages.title: Hansard — Feb 18 2026 Afternoon, Issue No. 118
passages.quote: That means fewer dollars available for long-term-care beds, health care recruitment, infrastructure and, certainly, education. Debt interest payments are becoming one of the largest spending items in government, only behind health and education, and this trajectory is simply unsustainable. It makes it clear that British Columbians simply can’t afford more of this NDP government. Now, as a former chamber of commerce president, I can tell you that this is one of the most concerning provincial budgets I’ve seen in several years for small businesses.

passages.title: Former rodeo rider Doerkson seeks to buck-off Eby (Hope Standard/CP)
passages.quote: Doerkson couldn’t articulate what he would do if that opposition grew into protests and blockades. Similarly, on reducing the growing budget deficit, he stuck to the standard Conservative lines about boosting economic productivity through deregulation, while steering clear of talk of spending cuts. Doerkson argues that the “simplest of things” are holding back the economy, such as the regulatory hoops companies must go through to harvest burnt wood after a wildfire. He said he wants a balanced budget “immediately,” even though he acknowledges that he doesn’t know what that path back to balance would look like without seeing the government’s complete books.

passages.title: Hansard — Feb 18 2026 Afternoon, Issue No. 118
passages.quote: Again, British Columbians and myself are asking: where has all the money gone? Well, let’s look at record spending, record debt and record disappointment. Government spending has exploded from $52 billion in 2017 to nearly $98.8 billion today, a 90 percent increase in less than a decade. The bureaucracy has grown dramatically — tens of thousands of additional full-time-equivalent positions over the past decade — yet this budget now proposes cutting 15,000 FTEs without any credible or transparent plan.

passages.title: Hansard — Feb 18 2026 Afternoon, Issue No. 118
passages.quote: So while the government promises no cuts to front-line services, it quietly chips away at school budgets instead. Education spending continues to fall as both a percentage of operating spending and a percentage of B.C.’s gross domestic product. In 2026-27, this coming fiscal, the provincial government will spend 4.3 percent of GDP on education — on the most important component in building the type of future workforce, skilled workforce and healthy, well-supported families that are needed for us to prosper as a province. And 4.3 percent is a shockingly low number.

passages.title: Economic, budget promises the focus of week 2 of B.C. election campaign (Global News)
passages.quote: The interim leader, who replaced Kerry-Lynne Findlay about a week ago following her resignation, pointed to an accounting error by the provincial government that overstated forecast revenues from natural gas by nearly $1.5 billion. “It’s going to be almost impossible to commit to how quickly we will be able to arrive at balanced budgets,” he said. “But the reality is, we have to get back to that.” Doerkson’s promised on Sunday that his government would not raise existing taxes or introduce new ones. Story continues below advertisement Eby said the promise of a tax freeze shows the Conservatives are not transparent about their plans.

passages.title: B.C. Conservative leader pledges to triple LNG production (Black Press)
passages.quote: “When you look at our plan — a real plan — we are going to be not only tripling but more than tripling LNG production by 2035,” Parmar said. Doerkson’s plan comes as provincial election campaign narratives have shifted on both the blue and orange sides toward affordability, with the Conservative Party leaning into a “no new taxes” message and the NDP warning those plans would require spending cuts. To make this point, NDP researchers dug up comments made by B.C. Conservative MLA Tony Luck in February, in which he said health and education would need to be cut because they are the biggest budgetary line items.
